related_questions.snippet: About 4 percent of women who have lichen sclerosus will develop vulvar cancer. related_questions.question: Can you recover from vulvar cancer?
related_questions.snippet: If you've been diagnosed with advanced vulval cancer, it may be hard to treat and not possible to cure. The aim of treatment will be to slow down the growth and spread of the cancer, to help with the symptoms, and help you live longer. Finding out cancer cannot be cured can be very hard news to take in.

text_blocks.snippet: Vulvar cancer is a rare type of cancer that develops on the vulva, the external female genital organs. It typically grows slowly, with symptoms often appearing as a lump, itching, or changes in skin color or texture. Early detection and treatment are crucial, and surgery is often the primary treatment method.
snippet_highlighted_words: a rare type of cancer that develops on the vulva, the external female genital organs

list.title: Rare Cancer:
list.snippet: Vulvar cancer accounts for a small percentage of all cancers in women.

list.title: Slow Growth:
list.snippet: It often develops over several years, starting with precancerous changes in the vulvar skin.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Common symptoms include a lump or mass on the vulva, persistent itching or pain, bleeding that is not from menstruation, and changes in skin color or texture.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: A physical exam, biopsy of any suspicious tissue, and other imaging tests may be used to diagnose vulvar cancer.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Surgery is the main treatment, often involving removal of the cancerous tissue and sometimes surrounding tissue or lymph nodes.

list.title: HPV and Risk Factors:
list.snippet: HPV infection and increasing age are significant risk factors for vulvar cancer.

list.title: Survival Rates:
list.snippet: Survival rates vary depending on the stage of the cancer at diagnosis, with localized cancer having a better prognosis than cancer that has spread.

list.title: Importance of Early Detection:
list.snippet: Early detection and treatment are vital for improving survival and minimizing the extent of treatment required.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary: Vulvar cancer is a rare but treatable cancer of the external female genitalia, with symptoms often developing gradually. Early diagnosis and treatment, often involving surgery, are key to a positive outcome.
